correctness.rationale: For each marked point a, distinct traces containing a require distinct neighbors of a. Hence the incidence budget is md, and the minimum incidence cost for a fixed number of nonempty traces is attained by buying sets in increasing cardinality. If r<m, maximality of r gives rho < C(m-1,r), so the prescribed residual count does not exceed the available (r+1)-layer. Minimizing the square-sum of degrees in that uniform layer proves the claimed balancing: edges through both points cancel from the degree difference, so a higher-to-lower swap with an absent replacement exists whenever the difference is at least two. The resulting maximum extra incidence is ceil((r+1)e/m) <= rho. Every selected trace size is itself at most d. For a minimum host, the isolated singleton, matching (with at most one isolate), edge, triangle, and path on at least four points cover the stated cases and give distinct marked traces of permitted sizes. Adding just the missing traces as unmarked vertices makes each marked degree exactly its frequency among the traces and each unmarked degree its trace size. This also proves attainability for all saturation cases, and d=0 separately requires only the m isolated marked vertices. At a threshold the cheapest full layers exhaust the budget, and omitting the empty trace or substituting any larger set is impossible in an extremal family. Shattering is therefore possible exactly at d >= 2^(m-1); the large-m linear formula gives density one for fixed d>0. No required computation underlies these conclusions. The supplied check.py and VERIFICATION.md were inspected, not run; their enumerations and construction checks are finite diagnostics, and the listed expected output is not an independent run.
